- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and model shows strong upward bias, cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high to avoid overcorrection.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% above true peak); apply a 3–5 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 2–4% per day post-spike.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.33 to 0.67), model tends to overreact; dampen forecast by 3–5% for 2–3 days following sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above 18-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–3% downward adjustment for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 0.33, 0.67, 0.33), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 2–4% for 3–5 days after such pattern.
